quote: I was just reaching out because it looks like we built up a solar design for you that we weren't able to go to quite yet. Does that sound familiar?
stewart_read: The customer reveals three different solar companies visited around the same time, one possibly also pitching a water softener — real competitive intelligence — but the rep only asks if it was 'at the same time' rather than which companies or what was proposed.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this detail irrelevant since Ion already had a design built and the goal was just re-engagement, not competitive analysis.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to spend 10-15 seconds probing 'which companies were those?' — that context is valuable for the closer walking into a crowded competitive field.

quote: I will say just before you kinda dismiss it completely, I know solar in the past kinda wasn't an extra bill.
stewart_read: This is a partial inversion — the rep reframes solar as a bill swap rather than an added cost, which is the right strategy, but he never anchors it to the customer's actual bill number since none was captured, softening the impact.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be intentionally avoiding a bill ask given the customer already said they don't have one settled yet post-move, making the generic swap framing the practical choice here.
coaching_implication: Note that the swap reframe worked as a strategy match even without a number — but flag that no bill amount was ever asked for, weakening how concrete this reframe could have been.

quote: No. It's just something I'm I'm gonna have to discuss with my my other half.
stewart_read: This is the textbook spouse-decision protocol trigger. The rep's immediate response is 'For sure, for sure' followed by a scarcity-close about the calendar filling up rather than the schema's correct pattern of directly proposing a joint time.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep does partially recover at 03:44 by mentioning 'we could call you and your partner,' so this may be a delayed rather than fully missed execution of the protocol.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to lead with the partner-inclusion question immediately when the spouse line is raised, rather than routing through a scarcity close first.

quote: we could do a phone call appointment where we could call you and your partner and then have you
stewart_read: This is the rep's actual attempt at spouse-inclusion protocol, but it is garbled mid-sentence and never becomes a clean confirmed ask ('what time works for both of you?'). It softens — but does not resolve — the earlier miss at 02:50.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep stumbled into the right words without a deliberate structured ask, given the sentence trails off uncompleted.
coaching_implication: Show the rep this exact clip: the instinct was there, but the delivery needs to land as a clear, complete question confirming both parties will be present.

quote: Alright. Why don't we do this? Is there any way you can email me and just so I can discuss it? I'm driving right now.
stewart_read: Customer attempts a soft exit combining a driving excuse and an email request; the rep correctly declines the email-only path and redirects to a phone appointment, holding the hard rule.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a real objection (email is easier) rather than a protocol/hard-rule situation, but the schema explicitly treats proposal-by-email as a hard rule, not a persuasion target.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as a correct execution — the rep should be told this line-holding was good and repeatable.

quote: I think we'll have our our specialist come by just because, you know, phone call is kind of our last resort.
stewart_read: The customer explicitly said phone call would 'always be better' at 04:13, and the rep books it as a phone appointment through the day/time negotiation, but then reverses to in-person at the very end without re-confirming with the customer or asking 'is that fair?'
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may believe in-person conversion rates are structurally higher and is upgrading the appointment type, which is a legitimate business judgment, not a lapse.
coaching_implication: Flag the channel-flip as a booking fragility risk — the customer may show up expecting a call, not a doorstep visit, which risks a no-show or confusion. Coach the rep to either confirm the channel change explicitly with the customer or not change it unilaterally.
